reason: The cited evidence (E1) directly supports that 0.5 at.% interstitial N increases SFE in a CoCrNi medium entropy alloy, but it does not address grain boundary cohesion, the effect on an order–disorder transition, or the specific (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 system. The premises on grain boundary cohesion and minimal caloric impact are unsupported by the cited passage.
premises: Interstitial N increases stacking fault energy (SFE) in multi-principal-element alloys
0.5 at.% N raises SFE substantially (e.g., by ~240%)
Higher SFE reduces dislocation dissociation and premature crack initiation, improving toughness
Interstitial N enhances grain boundary cohesion
The order–disorder transition responsible for the caloric effect is minimally affected by N doping
